**Continuous 2.38.11**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.38.10, 2.38.9, 2.38.8, 2.38.7, 2.38.6, 2.38.5, 2.38.4, 2.38.3, 2.38.2, 2.38.1, 2.38.0, 2.36.0, 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.38.11.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                         |
| --------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.38.11.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.38.11.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.38.11.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.38.11.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.38.11.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.38.11.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.38.11-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.38.11.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.38.11-vscode/continuous-cli-2.38.11.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.38.10

IDGAF is now a preset, not a level. It is Permissive with every safety check turned off, and each check follows its own switch. Questions gets a new level, Delegate. Five checks you could not turn off separately now have switches of their own.

### New

- **Delegate on Questions.** At Delegate the agent decides every question itself, from the options it was given, and each answer is recorded in the audit trail. It is a level of Questions only: it is not offered for any other area, and a settings file that sets it on another area is read as the default for that area.
- **Five more switches in Settings > Permissions > Protections**, all on unless you turn them off: **Apply my deny, ask and floor rules**, **Hold changes in Plan mode**, **Ask before an oddly spelled file name**, **Refuse unsafe fetch targets** and **Ask before using an MCP tool you have not approved**. **Ask before a command writes to a path built when it runs** is also there and is off until you turn it on. Before, the level decided these, so the only way to relax one was to relax all of them. **Never change the permission files** was already a switch; under the IDGAF preset it is now off like the rest.
- **The IDGAF preset sets the checks, and you can turn any one back on.** Choose it in Settings > Permissions, `/policy idgaf` or `--policy idgaf`. With one check back on, the preset shows as Custom, not IDGAF, and that check works as it says.

### Behaviour changes

- **IDGAF is saved like any other preset.** It used to last one session and was never written to `permissions.yaml`. Now `/policy idgaf --yes` and the preset in Settings keep it, with its levels and its switches,. `--auto` and `--policy idgaf` on the command line still last for that run only.
- **A saved `idgaf` or `yolo` level is read as Permissive** (Delegate on Questions) and written back under its current name.
- **The levels no longer decide whether a check runs.** Plan mode holds a change that would run, at every level, until you turn off "Hold changes in Plan mode". A rule you wrote is read at every level until you turn off "Apply my deny, ask and floor rules".
- **The protections list counts 17.** It said "11 of 11 on", and the new switches are in the count.
- **`--auto` carries the preset's switches to the loop's workers.** A worker is a separate process and saw only the levels, so a loop started with `--auto` would have started asking in its workers.
- **`cn doctor config` names where each check's setting came from**, including `--auto` and `--policy <preset>`.

### Removed

- **"IDGAF ran this past a rule" is gone.** A check that is off does not run, so there is nothing to record as run past, and a call is no longer held for a countdown because it ran past one. Audit lines written by earlier versions are still read, and `numIdgafObjections` stays in the `result` event of `--output-format stream-json`, always 0, so a script that reads it keeps working.

### Fixes

- **The save guards in VS Code and IntelliJ know the levels.** IntelliJ rejected a Questions level of Delegate, and both accepted Delegate for tools. IntelliJ also ranked Automatic below Permissive, which made some raises look like lowerings.
- **`--policy delegate` no longer sets Delegate on every area.** It is refused, and `questions=delegate` is the way to set it.
- **The note naming where an edit outside the workspace landed is back** for an allowed edit when its check is off. It was keyed on a level that no longer exists.
- **Dependencies:** `@anthropic-ai/sdk` 1.12, `openai` 7.62 (CLI), `google-auth-library` 11, `jsdom` 31, `@biomejs/biome` 2.6, `quick-lru` 8 and `dotenv` 18, plus the IntelliJ Gradle and the Rust `sync` updates. The `sync` crate is not built by the release, and nothing here compiled the two Cargo updates.
